digest.headline: RIDAR propose un cadre robuste pour détecter et corriger les violations d'intégrité dans les agents autonomes de recherche, marquant une avancée majeure en régulation des systèmes IA.
digest.overview: La veille du 2026-10-24 met en lumière des progrès significatifs dans la régulation, l'optimisation et l'architecture des systèmes IA, notamment pour les agents autonomes et les modèles de langage. Les travaux couvrent des enjeux techniques critiques, allant de la sécurité à l'efficacité computationnelle, tout en explorant des applications concrètes en santé et robotique.

highlights.title: RIDAR : Sécurisation des agents autonomes de recherche
highlights.text: Le framework RIDAR introduit une taxonomie de 14 types de violations d'intégrité de la recherche (RIV) et des outils de détection post-hoc (85.2% F1) et en temps réel (réduction de 36.8% des RIV). Il adresse un besoin croissant de régulation proactive dans les systèmes autonomes, où l'absence de garde-fous peut compromettre la fiabilité des résultats. Cette approche est particulièrement pertinente pour les agents déployés dans des domaines sensibles comme la recherche scientifique ou médicale.

highlights.title: Optimisation des modèles de diffusion pour le langage
highlights.text: Deux études complémentaires abordent l'optimisation des Diffusion Language Models (DLMs). T²Quant propose une quantification mixte sensible aux tâches et aux étapes de débruitage, améliorant la précision jusqu'à +6.7 points sous contrainte de bits fixes. Parallèlement, une analyse des politiques d'unmasking montre qu'une approche basée sur la contraction de trajectoire et la confiance réduit le NFE de 10% sans perte de précision. Ces travaux sont cruciaux pour rendre les DLMs plus efficaces et adaptables à des cas d'usage variés.

highlights.title: RouteWeaver et l'unification des modes d'exécution des LLM
highlights.text: RouteWeaver introduit un cadre unifié pour router dynamiquement les LLM en intégrant plusieurs modes d'exécution (single-round, multi-round, agentique) au sein d'une même politique. Optimisé via COMET-GRPO, il atteint 61% de précision moyenne sur 5 tâches de raisonnement, démontrant une avancée dans l'adaptabilité des agents LLM. Cette approche répond au défi de l'hétérogénéité des tâches, où un seul modèle doit gérer des exigences variées en termes de complexité et de latence.

highlights.title: Fuite de confidentialité et collaboration humain-agent
highlights.text: Agent Mosaic révèle des taux élevés de divulgation sensible dans les systèmes agents LLM via l'effet mosaïque, malgré les garde-fous existants. Parallèlement, une étude sur la collaboration humain-agent montre que les modèles plus performants optimisent la division du travail mais réduisent leur dépendance à l'humain. Ces travaux soulignent les enjeux de sécurité et d'interaction dans les systèmes hybrides, où la confiance et la transparence restent des défis majeurs.

highlights.title: Outils et frameworks pour la robotique et la chimie computationnelle
highlights.text: TARSphere propose un framework full-stack pour agents robotiques en environnements dynamiques, combinant simulateur physique et MLLM gelé. MolLean, quant à lui, introduit un langage vérifiable pour le raisonnement chimique, intégrant des vérifications de cohérence moléculaire en temps réel. Ces outils illustrent l'importance de l'intégration entre modèles de langage et domaines spécialisés, où la précision et la vérifiabilité sont critiques.

digest.trend: Les avancées récentes confirment une tendance vers des systèmes IA plus régulés, optimisés et intégrés, avec une attention accrue portée à la sécurité, à l'efficacité computationnelle et à l'interopérabilité avec des domaines spécialisés. L'autonomie des agents et leur collaboration avec les humains restent des axes de recherche prioritaires, tout en nécessitant des mécanismes de contrôle et de transparence renforcés.

items.title: RIDAR: Safeguarding Research Integrity in Autonomous Research Agents via Automated Detection and Runtime Intervention
items.summary: Autonomous research agents are increasingly used to automate large portions of scientific research, yet they are prone to research integrity violations (RIVs): behaviors that compromise the validity, reproducibility, or faithfulness of the research process. We present RIDAR, a framework for automated RIV detection and runtime intervention. First, we introduce RIVT, a comprehensive taxonomy of 14 RIV types spanning the full research lifecycle. Building on RIVT, we present RIDAR-post-hoc, a framework to detect RIVs within agent trajectories. RIDAR-post-hoc achieves 85.2% F1 performance on RIV-Gold, a benchmark for RIV detection with 60 expert-annotated trajectories. Applying RIDAR-post-hoc to RIV-Wild, a dataset of 300 agent trajectories across 50 distinct research tasks, we detect 3,964 RIV instances in 99.7% of trajectories, revealing the prevalence of RIVs in current agents. Finally, we present RIDAR-runtime, a framework for dynamically detecting and correcting RIVs during agent runtime. RIDAR-runtime effectively reduces agent RIVs remaining at task completion by 36.8%. We will release our code and data to facilitate future research.
items.tldr: Framework RIDAR pour détecter et corriger automatiquement les violations d'intégrité de la recherche (RIV) dans les agents autonomes, avec une taxonomie de 14 types de RIV et des outils de détection post-hoc (85.2% F1) et en temps réel (réduction de 36.8% des RIV).

deep_analysis.probleme: Cette publication aborde le défi croissant des violations de l'intégrité de la recherche (RIV) dans les agents autonomes de recherche scientifique. Ces agents, de plus en plus utilisés pour automatiser des étapes clés du processus scientifique, peuvent générer des comportements compromettant la validité, la reproductibilité ou la fidélité des résultats, posant ainsi un risque majeur pour la crédibilité de la recherche automatisée.

methode.taxonomie: Les auteurs introduisent RIVT, une taxonomie exhaustive de 14 types de violations de l'intégrité de la recherche, couvrant l'ensemble du cycle de vie d'un projet scientifique. Cette classification sert de base pour structurer la détection et l'intervention.
methode.detection_post_hoc: Le framework RIDAR-post-hoc est conçu pour détecter les RIV dans les trajectoires d'agents déjà exécutées. Il s'appuie sur RIV-Gold, un benchmark annoté par des experts (60 trajectoires), pour évaluer ses performances. Les détails techniques précis (modèles utilisés, approches d'annotation, ou algorithmes de détection) ne sont pas explicitement décrits dans le résumé disponible.
methode.intervention_runtime: RIDAR-runtime étend cette approche en intégrant une détection et une correction dynamiques des RIV pendant l'exécution des agents. Le système semble agir en temps réel pour identifier et corriger les comportements problématiques, bien que les mécanismes exacts (ex. : règles prédéfinies, apprentissage par renforcement, ou autres) ne soient pas détaillés.

resultats.performance_detection: RIDAR-post-hoc atteint un score F1 de 85,2 % sur le benchmark RIV-Gold, démontrant une capacité robuste à identifier les RIV dans des trajectoires annotées.
resultats.prevalence_des_RIV: L'application de RIDAR-post-hoc à RIV-Wild, un jeu de données de 300 trajectoires d'agents sur 50 tâches de recherche distinctes, révèle 3 964 instances de RIV dans 99,7 % des trajectoires, soulignant l'omniprésence du problème.
resultats.efficacite_intervention: RIDAR-runtime réduit de 36,8 % le nombre de RIV restantes à la fin des tâches, prouvant son utilité pour atténuer les risques en temps réel.

limites.manque_de_details_techniques: Le résumé ne fournit pas d'informations précises sur les modèles ou algorithmes sous-jacents (ex. : apprentissage supervisé, règles heuristiques, ou hybridation), ce qui limite l'évaluation de la robustesse ou de la généralisabilité de l'approche.
limites.biais_potentiels: Les résultats dépendent fortement de la qualité des annotations dans RIV-Gold et RIV-Wild, ainsi que de la représentativité des tâches sélectionnées. Une validation sur des cas réels ou des domaines variés serait nécessaire pour confirmer l'efficacité du framework.
limites.correction_runtime: Bien que RIDAR-runtime réduise les RIV, le résumé ne précise pas si les corrections introduisent d'autres biais ou si elles altèrent la performance globale des agents (ex. : ralentissement, perte de créativité).

deep_analysis.verdict: Cette publication mérite une attention particulière pour son approche systématique et ses résultats prometteurs, mais son adoption dépendra de la transparence des détails techniques et de sa validation sur des scénarios réels et variés.

items.title: Different Tasks, Different Timesteps: Temporal Task-Aware Quantization for Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) introduce unique quantization challenges due to their iterative denoising process. In this work, we reveal that quantization sensitivity is both taskand time-dependent, with different downstream tasks exhibiting distinct precision requirements across denoising steps. We further show that these patterns can be predicted without groundtruth labels or task-specific evaluation metrics. Building on these findings, we introduce T 2Quant, a task and time-aware mixedprecision quantization framework that uses a label-free sensitivity signal to optimally allocate activation precision across denoising steps under a fixed bit-width budget. Extensive experiments across three DLMs and six benchmarks demonstrate that T 2Quant consistently improves the average accuracy of existing quantization methods, achieving gains of up to 6.7 percentage points under the same budget.
items.tldr: T²Quant introduit une quantification mixte sensible aux tâches et aux étapes de débruitage pour les DLMs, améliorant la précision jusqu'à +6.7 points sous contrainte de bits fixes. Résultat clé pour l'optimisation efficace des DLMs.

deep_analysis.probleme: Les modèles de langage basés sur la diffusion (DLMs) présentent des défis uniques en matière de quantification en raison de leur processus itératif de débruitage. La sensibilité à la quantification varie non seulement selon les tâches, mais aussi au fil des étapes de débruitage, ce qui complique l'optimisation des performances sous des contraintes de précision fixe.
deep_analysis.methode: Les auteurs proposent T²Quant, un cadre de quantification mixte sensible à la tâche et au temps. Ce framework identifie des motifs de sensibilité à la quantification sans recourir à des étiquettes de vérité terrain ou à des métriques spécifiques aux tâches. Il utilise un signal de sensibilité sans label pour allouer dynamiquement la précision des activations à travers les étapes de débruitage, tout en respectant un budget de bits fixe. L'approche exploite des observations empiriques sur la variabilité des besoins en précision selon les tâches et les timesteps.
deep_analysis.resultats: Les expériences menées sur trois modèles DLMs et six benchmarks montrent que T²Quant améliore systématiquement la précision moyenne des méthodes de quantification existantes, avec des gains allant jusqu'à 6,7 points de pourcentage sous le même budget de bits. Les résultats confirment l'efficacité de l'allocation dynamique de précision.
deep_analysis.limites: Le contenu disponible ne précise pas les détails techniques du signal de sensibilité sans label, ni les critères exacts d'allocation de bits. De plus, l'impact de T²Quant sur la latence ou la complexité computationnelle n'est pas abordé, ce qui limite l'évaluation de sa faisabilité pratique.
deep_analysis.verdict: Ce travail mérite une attention particulière pour son approche innovante de quantification adaptative, mais nécessite des validations supplémentaires sur des cas d'usage réels et des analyses de coût.

items.title: What Makes a Good Unmasking Policy? A Controlled Study of Learned Unmasking in Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: Masked diffusion language models generate tokens in parallel, but their efficiency depends on which predictions are committed. Learned unmasking policies improve the speed--accuracy trade-off, yet differ in supervision, inputs, and capacity, obscuring which choices matter. We view supervised policies as distilling a decoding procedure through a teacher and examine independently what the teacher labels as committable, on which states the policy imitates it, what the policy observes, and how much the number of function evaluations (NFE) must decrease to offset policy overhead. We find that labeling predictions matching the final output is overly permissive at low NFE, and hidden states are weak alone but can complement confidence. About a 10% NFE reduction suffices to offset policy overhead for policies up to 7.5M parameters across tested settings. We therefore train a policy on trajectory-contraction targets, which accept only commitments staying on a reference trajectory, using confidence and hidden states. On LLaDA-8B-Instruct, the resulting 856K-parameter policy achieves the best accuracy--NFE frontier and highest throughput on GSM8K, is competitive at moderate targets on MATH-500 and HumanEval, and largely transfers to Dream-7B-Instruct.
items.tldr: Étude des politiques d'unmasking dans les modèles de diffusion pour le langage, montrant qu'une politique basée sur la contraction de trajectoire et la confiance réduit le NFE de 10% sans perte de précision. Optimisation du trade-off vitesse-précision.

deep_analysis.probleme: Les modèles de langage à diffusion masquée génèrent des tokens en parallèle, mais leur efficacité dépend fortement de la stratégie utilisée pour décider quelles prédictions peuvent être validées (unmasking). Une politique d'unmasking sous-optimale peut dégrader le compromis vitesse-précision, un enjeu critique pour les applications en temps réel ou à grande échelle.
deep_analysis.methode: Les auteurs abordent ce problème en étudiant systématiquement les politiques d'unmasking *apprises*, qui imitent une procédure de décodage supervisée (un *teacher*). Ils analysent quatre dimensions clés : (1) **la définition des cibles** (quels tokens le *teacher* considère comme committables, par exemple ceux correspondant à la sortie finale ou à une trajectoire de référence), (2) **les états observés** par la politique (confiance du modèle, états cachés, ou une combinaison), (3) **la supervision** (comment le *teacher* est utilisé pour entraîner la politique), et (4) **le compromis surcoût/NFE** (réduction minimale du nombre d'évaluations de fonction, NFE, nécessaire pour compenser le coût de la politique). Ils proposent une cible de *trajectory-contraction*, où seuls les tokens restant sur une trajectoire de référence sont validés, et entraînent une politique légère (856K paramètres) combinant confiance et états cachés.
deep_analysis.resultats: La politique optimisée atteint le meilleur compromis précision-NFE sur le benchmark GSM8K avec le modèle LLaDA-8B-Instruct, tout en offrant le débit le plus élevé. Elle reste compétitive sur MATH-500 et HumanEval pour des cibles de précision modérées, et montre une bonne transférabilité vers Dream-7B-Instruct. Les auteurs observent qu'une réduction d'environ 10% du NFE suffit à compenser le surcoût de politiques allant jusqu'à 7,5M paramètres. Ils notent aussi que les cibles basées sur la sortie finale sont trop permissives à faible NFE, tandis que les états cachés seuls sont peu informatifs mais utiles en complément de la confiance.
deep_analysis.limites: L'étude se concentre sur des modèles et benchmarks spécifiques (principalement LLaDA-8B et Dream-7B), limitant la généralisabilité des conclusions. Le choix de la trajectoire de référence pour la *trajectory-contraction* pourrait introduire un biais dépendant du *teacher* utilisé. Enfin, l'impact des politiques d'unmasking sur des tâches plus complexes ou des modèles plus grands reste à explorer.
deep_analysis.verdict: Ce travail mérite l'attention pour son analyse rigoureuse des politiques d'unmasking et ses résultats prometteurs sur le compromis vitesse-précision, bien que des validations supplémentaires soient nécessaires pour confirmer sa robustesse.

items.title: RouteWeaver: Weaving Mode Selection and Execution into Unified LLM Routing
items.summary: LLM routing dynamically selects and coordinates heterogeneous language models across diverse tasks. However, existing approaches are largely built around a predefined execution paradigm, such as single-round, multi-round, or agentic routing, which fixes how model calls are organized and limits adaptation to different query needs. We propose RouteWeaver, a unified routing framework that integrates these routing modes within a single LLM policy, jointly learning which mode to use and how to select models within that mode. To jointly optimize mode selection and within-mode execution, we develop COMET-GRPO (COordinated Mode-Execution Training), which decouples the trajectory-level advantage into separate signals for mode selection and within-mode execution, enabling more targeted credit assignment to each decision level. We further introduce progressive exploration, which gradually shifts training from externally assigned modes to autonomous selection, so that the router first learns how to execute each mode before deciding when to use it. We evaluate RouteWeaver across mathematics, coding, knowledge, logical reasoning, and factual recall. RouteWeaver achieves an average accuracy of 61.4%, an 11.03% relative improvement over the strongest baseline, and outperforms all compared baselines in each of the five domains. Ablations show that both COMET-GRPO and progressive exploration are important for adaptive routing; without progressive exploration, the routing policy collapses entirely to single-round execution.
items.tldr: RouteWeaver propose un cadre unifié pour router dynamiquement les LLM en intégrant plusieurs modes d'exécution (single-round, multi-round, agentique) au sein d'une même politique, optimisé via COMET-GRPO pour une sélection autonome et une exécution ciblée. Évalué sur 5 tâches de raisonnement, il atteint 61% de précision moyenne, démontrant une avancée dans l'adaptabilité des agents LLM.

deep_analysis.probleme: Les systèmes actuels de routage d'IA pour les modèles de langage (LLM) reposent sur des paradigmes d'exécution prédéfinis (ex. : requête unique, multi-tours, ou routage agentique), ce qui limite leur capacité à s'adapter dynamiquement aux besoins variés des tâches. Cette rigidité empêche une optimisation conjointe du choix du mode d'exécution et de la sélection des modèles, réduisant ainsi l'efficacité globale du routage.
deep_analysis.methode: RouteWeaver propose un cadre unifié intégrant plusieurs modes de routage (single-round, multi-round, agentique) au sein d'une seule politique LLM. Pour optimiser conjointement la sélection du mode et l'exécution intra-mode, les auteurs introduisent COMET-GRPO (COordinated Mode-Execution Training), une méthode qui décompose l'avantage au niveau de la trajectoire en signaux distincts pour chaque niveau de décision. Cela permet une attribution plus ciblée des récompenses. Par ailleurs, une stratégie de *progressive exploration* est utilisée : l'entraînement commence par des modes assignés de manière externe avant de passer à une sélection autonome, permettant au routeur d'apprendre d'abord à exécuter chaque mode avant de décider quand l'utiliser.
deep_analysis.resultats: RouteWeaver atteint une précision moyenne de 61,4 % sur cinq domaines (mathématiques, codage, connaissances, raisonnement logique, rappel factuel), soit une amélioration relative de 11,03 % par rapport au meilleur baseline. Il surpasse tous les baselines dans chacun des domaines évalués. Les ablations montrent que COMET-GRPO et la *progressive exploration* sont cruciaux pour un routage adaptatif : sans cette dernière, la politique de routage s'effondre en un mode d'exécution single-round exclusif.
deep_analysis.limites: Le contenu disponible ne précise pas les détails sur la complexité computationnelle de COMET-GRPO ni sur les coûts d'entraînement, ce qui pourrait limiter son applicabilité à grande échelle. De plus, l'évaluation se concentre sur des tâches académiques ou contrôlées, sans garantie de généralisation à des scénarios réels plus bruités ou imprévisibles.
deep_analysis.verdict: RouteWeaver mérite une attention particulière pour son approche innovante et ses résultats prometteurs, mais son adoption dépendra de sa scalabilité et de sa robustesse en conditions réelles.

items.title: Agent Mosaic: Recognizing Confidentiality Leaks in Agentic LLM Systems
items.summary: Modern LLM agents can retrieve information from accessible documents, and then disclose a sensitive conclusion assembled from them. This mosaic effect creates a critical risk for agents operating over confidential data. We quantify its realization with 30 synthetic cybersecurity, medical, and military examples, yielding 10,800 final answers from three LLM agents in controlled simulation and 1,440 answers from live agents in two open-source harnesses. Even under benign queries designed to be answerable from one document, GPT-5.6-Sol, the best performing model tested, discloses forbidden composites in 7.08% of answers (95% CI: 3.75-10.67%) in simulation, with worse disclosure rates in live harnesses. Adding visible classification headers and explicit aggregation rules reduces pooled disclosure rates substantially, yet unsafe disclosures persist in 32.37% of simulated answers (95% CI: 28.33-36.19%) across all intents despite these safeguards. Furthermore, increased refusals do not guarantee confidentiality, since significant refusals reveal the prohibited conclusion regardless. These results point to a troubling conclusion: sensitive data leaks via mosaic-style events are an observed confidentiality failure mode in the evaluated settings at non-negligible rates. They motivate stronger controls on what agents may infer and disclose in sensitive data environments with mixed-clearance users.
items.tldr: Agent Mosaic quantifie les fuites de confidentialité via l'effet mosaïque dans les systèmes agents LLM, révélant des taux de divulgation sensibles élevés malgré des garde-fous. Critique pour la sécurité et la conformité des agents IA.

items.title: Who Takes the Lead? Model Ability and Task-Conditioned Collaboration with Humans
items.summary: As language-model agents grow more capable, they can carry more of a task without asking anyone for help. Falling reliance on a human partner is easy to read as a failure of collaboration when it may instead be a correct division of labor, and the rate of human involvement alone cannot tell the two apart. We study this systematically by placing an agent and a person under a shared objective while varying who holds the advantage: the human has a clear advantage, neither does, or the agent does. To obtain this control, we introduce a shared-control maze, in which an agent-controlled and a human-controlled avatar share the objective of reaching a common target in as few team turns as possible. The agent allocates each team turn between acting itself and handing the move to the person, and initial placement sets the human's shortest-path advantage while the task is otherwise unchanged. We evaluate GPT~5.6~Sol, Command~A+, Qwen~3.8~27B, and Command~R, first measuring solo capability with a single avatar and full-map observability, then running co-play with human participants across the three advantage conditions. Across the four models, stronger solo performance is associated with selective, route-conditioned human involvement: the models that solve the maze reliably on their own act for themselves almost without exception when the human holds no advantage, and involve the human on roughly 80% of initial decisions when the human route is shorter. Command R, the model with substantially weaker solo performance, shows no such selectivity.
items.tldr: Étude systématique de la collaboration humain-agent dans un environnement de résolution de labyrinthe, montrant que les modèles plus performants seuls réduisent leur dépendance à l'humain, mais optimisent la division du travail. Analyse basée sur 4 modèles (GPT-5.6-Sol, Command-A+, Qwen3.8-27B, Command-R) et des participants humains.

items.title: MolLean: A Process-Verifiable Language for Chemical Reasoning
items.summary: Chemical chain-of-thought can contain hallucinated structural and property claims. We thereby introduce MolLean, a process-verifiable language that grounds chemical reasoning in an explicit molecular state. A layered Lean-based kernel checks state transitions and assertions over molecular readouts, from primitive graph edits to compound transformations. Meanwhile, a typed witness protocol separates native structural checks from externally supplied measurements. We further introduce MolLean-MCP, a stateful tool interface that exposes these transitions, checks, and readouts during generation: the model receives feedback to decide its next action, and rejected actions leave the state unchanged. MolLean supports one-pass trace execution, whole-trace refinement, and interactive reasoning through MolLean-MCP. We evaluate these three modes with direct chain-of-thought on 8,800 matched examples across 12 tasks spanning molecular generation, editing, optimization, and reactions. With Qwen3.6-27B, whole-trace refinement outperforms direct chain-of-thought on all 12 tasks. MolLean-MCP complements whole-trace refinement with stepwise verification feedback, reaching better performance in reaction tasks. Together, these results highlight an executable foundation for chemical reasoning, in which explicit chemical commitments can be checked and revised rather than remaining solely in free-form explanations.
items.tldr: MolLean introduit un langage vérifiable (Lean-based) pour le raisonnement chimique, intégrant des vérifications de cohérence moléculaire en temps réel via un protocole témoin typé. Avec MolLean-MCP, il permet une interaction itérative et une correction des hallucinations, surpassant les approches directes sur 12 tâches de chimie computationnelle.

items.title: Inherited, Not Invented: Tracing the Provenance of Wait in Reasoning Models
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) is credited with teaching reasoning models to write {wait} before reconsidering a step, yet large RL accuracy gains do not require the word. This view can confuse what RL discovers with what a model inherits from its training data. We trace the word through open models' training histories, reading it with label-free indices of frequency, position, form and usage and an injected-error test, all computed from sampled outputs. We find that zero-RL almost never coins the marker: on bases that lack the word, RL raises MATH-500 accuracy substantially while {wait} stays near absent. It arrives with training data: mid-training in OLMo-3, and fine-tuning on reasoning traces installs it in most models whose base lacks it. Where the base already uses it, both released RL-Zero recipes (OLMo-3, MiMo) multiply it, whereas KL-free GRPO from the same base does not; OLMo-3's recipe wears down its form and makes it a more sensitive but more liberal alarm; RL after supervised fine-tuning barely changes it, and our GRPO recipe erases a marker seeded by fine-tuning. Finally, we show that marker frequency alone does not indicate RL-induced reasoning and caution against LLM-as-a-judge revision metrics, as automated judges can reverse human-labelled trends.
items.tldr: Cette étude démontre que le mot-clé {wait} dans les modèles de raisonnement est principalement hérité des données d'entraînement (fine-tuning, traces de raisonnement) et non induit par RL, remettant en cause son association systématique avec des gains de performance.

items.title: TARSphere: A Robot-Oriented Full-Stack Framework for Long-Horizon Embodied Agents in Evolving Physical and Social Environments
items.summary: Robots must act under physical and social constraints while adapting to changes in their environment and human needs. Existing embodied-agent systems often focus on specified goals or abstract execution into symbolic actions, limiting evaluation in an evolving world. We introduce TARSphere, a robot-oriented full-stack framework for physically and socially grounded long-horizon embodied agents. TARSphere-Infra runs robot policies in a physics simulator with embodied NPCs and constrained dialogue. An event-driven finite-state machine (FSM) uses completed actions and delivered information to update task states and evaluate outcomes. TARSphere-Harness, its embodied brain harness, lets a frozen multimodal large language model (MLLM) act through multi-level executable skills, using observations, hierarchical memory, and execution feedback to revise its decisions. On this foundation, agent-in-the-loop curation aligns task semantics, causal dependencies, and scene geometry to construct TARSphere-Bench: 360 episodes across 30 indoor scenes. Five paired conditions assess perceptual robustness, disruption adaptation, task update, human coordination, and intent understanding for navigate-and-report and fetch-and-deliver tasks. Our evaluation of 8 MLLMs shows that general-purpose models can outperform embodied models, while task updates and human interaction remain difficult. Frequent collisions and falls further motivate evaluating execution safety alongside task success, even with a shared action interface and decision budget.
items.tldr: TARSphere propose un framework full-stack pour agents robotiques en environnement physique et social évolutif, combinant un simulateur physique, une FSM événementielle et un MLLM gelé avec compétences exécutables hiérarchiques. Intéressant pour l'intégration LLM-agents-robotique et l'évaluation en conditions dynamiques.

items.title: WeVisOne-VL: Unified Visual Perception from Objects to Pixels
items.summary: Existing vision-language models (VLMs) remain unreliable for fine-grained visual perception. In this report, we present WeVisOne-VL (WeChat Vision All-in-One), a powerful VLM that unifies object-level and pixel-level perception through structured next-token prediction. It supports multiple visual tasks including object detection, referring localization, counting, OCR, segmentation, and matting, enabling localization at any user-specific granularity, from points and boxes to masks and alpha mattes. Architecturally, we integrate a lightweight pixel decoder into the VLM via a special token to generate instance-level pixel outputs. We train the model with a three-stage curriculum SFT followed by mixed-task RL. Across over 30 benchmarks, WeVisOne-VL demonstrates leading performance on both object-level and pixel-level tasks, while maintaining robust rejection for object-absent queries. By releasing WeVisOne-VL to the open-source community, we hope to advance VLMs from broad visual understanding toward truly reliable perception systems for real-world deployment.
items.tldr: Modèle WeVisOne-VL unifiant perception visuelle objet et pixel via une prédiction structurée par tokens, supportant détection, segmentation, OCR et matting. Performant sur 30 benchmarks avec un entraînement en 3 étapes SFT + RL mixte.

items.title: The LLM-Attacker: A Unified Red-Team Framework for Privacy Evaluation of Split and Distributed LLM Systems
items.summary: Split language models keep input text on a client but send intermediate representations to a server. Attacks can reconstruct text from these messages. Comparing privacy evaluations is difficult when attackers see different messages, know different model weights or use different datasets and recovery measures. We present LLM-Attacker, a framework that records these choices and lets researchers check, compare and extend an evaluation. Compatible attacks reuse recorded messages, and their predictions are saved for independent scoring. The scoring rule requires a linked undefended reference before a defence can pass. Reports also identify attacks that remain untested. In a controlled GPT-2 experiment, adding gradients returned during training increased token recovery from 94.20% to 97.38% and exact-document recovery from 13.71% to 37.77%. The 95% interval for the token gain lay above the two-percentage-point threshold fixed before testing. This experiment is shared with a companion study; here, it tests how the evaluation responds to a change in attacker access. Further studies measure how corpus choice and compression defences affect recovery, compare an adapted published attack with its reference implementation, and test the measurement code. The framework reports implementation checks separately from measured attack effectiveness. Each privacy claim should state the attacker, dataset and scoring rule, report its controls and identify untested attacks.
items.tldr: LLM-Attacker standardise l'évaluation de la vie privée dans les modèles distribués (split LLMs) via un framework unifié pour comparer les attaques de reconstruction de texte. Pertinent pour la sécurité des LLM et l'optimisation des protocoles d'inférence distribuée.

items.title: SplatLab: Autonomous Scientific Discovery for 3DGS Research
items.summary: Reproducing a published 3DGS paper takes weeks of expert engineering before any extension can be proposed. Prior autonomous-research systems read papers, draft hypotheses, and write code, but are limited by short fixed templates, low executability, and weak traceability, and none has been demonstrated end-to-end in a live computer-vision subfield with intense activity. SplatLab is an autonomous research system for 3D Gaussian Splatting that addresses these limitations. Given a research prompt, a target-paper URL, or no input at all, it reproduces a published baseline, proposes an extension, trains and ablates across Mip-NeRF 360 and LLFF, writes the manuscript, and binds every reported number to a logged training run. Five design choices distinguish it: (i) candidates mutate plugins from a verified-reproduction backbone matched to published baselines; (ii) a cascade-weighted Elo tournament across eight islands scores candidates on measured GPU PSNR with verbal-gradient feedback; (iii) a standing falsifier subtracts Elo on failure, integrating stress-test survival into selection; (iv) every reported number is bound to a logged training run, and the run cannot terminate while any claim is unbacked; (v) a seven-category 3DGS taxonomy wraps EVOLVE-BLOCK markers in domain-aligned scaffolds transferable across 3DGS repositories. On PSNR-targeted runs, SplatLab's manuscripts beat their reproduced targets by +0.18 to +3.78 dB, including +3.78 dB on astrophotographic nebula rendering, for which no prior 3DGS method exists. The research cycle compresses from months of graduate-student time to days of mostly autonomous compute. Code, all manuscripts, experiment ledgers, and the cross-run paper store are available on the project page.
items.tldr: Système autonome (SplatLab) pour reproduire, étendre et documenter des recherches en 3D Gaussian Splatting, avec traçabilité intégrale des résultats et tournoi Elo pondéré pour évaluer les extensions. Démontre une autonomie complète dans un sous-domaine actif.

items.title: What Generation Knows: Unlocking Fine-Grained Understanding in Unified Multimodal Models
items.summary: Fine-grained visual understanding requires distinguishing subtle differences in local attributes and spatial relations, yet remains challenging for existing vision-language models. Unified multimodal models (UMMs) offer a new opportunity through generation pathways that preserve rich visual information complementary to understanding. However, existing generation-assisted understanding methods mainly rely on generative supervision or explicit generation and have not systematically explored direct use of native generation-side representations. To address this gap, we systematically analyze what generation-side representations offer for fine-grained understanding, finding that they are more sensitive to fine-grained semantic changes, capture task-relevant changes missed by understanding-side representations, and depend on correct spatial organization for this advantage. Guided by these findings, we design GAFU, a post-training framework that unlocks native generation-side information for fine-grained understanding. It compresses generation-side visual representations into compact \(G\) tokens that preserve fine-grained visual details, enabling task-conditioned retrieval by the understanding pathway. Experiments show that GAFU consistently outperforms SFT baselines trained on the same data across diverse visual understanding tasks and UMM architectures, with maximum relative improvements of 20.00\%, 17.94\%, and 8.62\% on VStar-Bench, OmniSpatial, and VSR-Bench, respectively. Overall, GAFU converts complementary information from the generation pathway into gains in fine-grained visual understanding, providing an effective path toward synergy between generation and understanding in UMMs.
items.tldr: Analyse des représentations génératives (GAFU) pour améliorer la compréhension fine-grained dans les modèles multimodaux unifiés. Montre que les tokens générés capturent mieux les détails sémantiques et spatiaux que les représentations dédiées.

items.title: RLSplat: Resource-Linear Budget Control for Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting
items.summary: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (FF3DGS) reconstructs 3D scenes from images in a single forward pass, making it well-suited to applications that must operate within limited resource budgets. To further improve its practicality, recent budget-controllable FF3DGS methods allow the number of Gaussians to be adjusted at inference, so that the output meets a given storage limit or rendering-latency constraint. However, these methods overlook the cost of inference itself: to produce a representation with the target number of Gaussians, they first predict a dense set of Gaussians and then prune or select from it, requiring nearly constant latency and peak memory regardless of the budget. We therefore propose RLSplat, a resource-linear budget-controllable FF3DGS framework whose representation size, inference latency, and peak memory all decrease linearly as the Gaussian budget is reduced. Instead of pruning or selection, RLSplat learns a Gaussian allocation policy that distributes the budget across local scene regions, so that exactly the requested number of Gaussians is generated. These Gaussians are then refined through resource-linear Gaussian decoding, in which each Gaussian attends only to nearby Gaussians found via an efficient hierarchical neighbor search, so that the decoding cost decreases linearly with fewer Gaussians. In zero-shot evaluation, RLSplat outperforms prior budget-controllable methods at every budget, surpassing the strongest baseline even with 4times fewer Gaussians, while running up to 4.1times faster with 9.6times less peak memory at low budgets.
items.tldr: Framework RLSplat pour un contrôle linéaire des ressources en 3D Gaussian Splatting feed-forward, réduisant linéairement la taille de la représentation, la latence et la mémoire avec le budget de Gaussiens. Alternative au pruning classique.

items.title: Editing Images into Reusable Layers via Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation
items.summary: High-quality image editing requires precise modification of target regions while preserving the content of unrelated regions. Existing editing models produce flattened outputs that limit precise local manipulation and layer reuse, while decomposition methods typically optimize layer recovery separately from instruction-driven editing. To this end, we introduce LayerEditor, a unified framework that couples instruction-guided image editing with controllable generation of reusable RGBA layers. At its core, In-Context RGB-Alpha Token Modeling jointly represents the edited canvas and an ordered sequence of RGB-Alpha layers within a single token sequence, enabling semantic edits and explicit control over individual layer content. To retain the pretrained model's editing capability during adaptation to layered outputs, we propose Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation, which transfers its editing prior to both the edited canvas and the image composed from the predicted layers. To support training and evaluation, we construct LayerEditor-100K, a large-scale paired image-editing dataset with ordered RGBA layer annotations, and introduce dedicated benchmarks for layered editing. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LayerEditor maintains strong editing fidelity while generating accurate RGBA layers, supporting both flexible layer-level manipulation and multi-layer decomposition.
items.tldr: LayerEditor introduit un cadre pour éditer des images en générant des couches RGBA réutilisables via une distillation prioritaire des capacités d'édition, combinant contrôle sémantique et préservation des régions non ciblées. Évalué sur un nouveau jeu de données (LayerEditor-100K), il permet une manipulation précise et réversible des images.

items.title: Bringing foundational models to the front lines of TB screening
items.summary: Generative AI
items.tldr: Application concrète d'un modèle de langage (LLM) pour le dépistage de la tuberculose via l'analyse d'images médicales, démontrant l'impact sociétal des modèles génératifs en santé publique.

items.title: Diffusion Language Models Change Speed Across Tasks and Languages
items.summary: Diffusion language models can write several tokens in one forward pass, and they decide during generation how many passes to spend. Two outputs of the same token length can therefore vary a lot in cost. To understand the underlying factors of this cost variation, we analyze two diffusion models across 10 tasks. We find that the number of forward passes per token depends heavily on the task. Text copied or lightly edited from the input is cheap, while open-ended writing is costly. In DiffusionGemma, generating a token for story writing requires more than three times as many forward passes as for grammar correction. Two output properties explain much of this gap: how much of it is new relative to the input, and how rare its words are within the task. The same holds within a single response when thinking is involved. The final answer is cheap when it repeats the model's reasoning trace and costly when it adds something new. In multilingual generation, we find that highly tokenized languages also require more passes per token, adding to the cost they already pay with more tokens. Finally, cost tracks correctness: on the same math problem, wrong answers take more passes per token than correct ones, and weighting candidate answers by decoding speed beats majority voting by up to 4.2 points at no extra cost. Taken together, our results show that diffusion's computational advantage depends on how much of the output is already determined, while its decoding effort offers a practical signal for making inference more efficient and reliable.
items.tldr: Les DLMs (Diffusion Language Models) ont des coûts de génération variables selon les tâches et langues, liés à la nouveauté et à la rareté des tokens. Analyse utile pour optimiser l'inférence et adapter les architectures aux cas d'usage.

items.title: IF-MAP: Influence-Function-Inspired Agent Prioritization in Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: Improving every agent in an LLM-based multi-agent system can be prohibitively costly, making it important to identify which agent should be prioritized to achieve the greatest system-level gain with limited resources. Failure attribution can inform this decision, but an agent's responsibility for failures does not directly reveal the system-level gains achievable by improving it. We therefore introduce IF-MAP, an influence-function-inspired method for identifying agents with high potential for system-level improvement. For each agent, IF-MAP measures end-to-end loss changes under controlled semantic prompt perturbations, fits a regularized local response model in a low-dimensional prompt-embedding subspace, and uses the estimated response norm as a priority score. This black-box procedure requires no access to model parameters or gradients and produces agent priorities that can guide subsequent improvement effort. We evaluate IF-MAP across six multi-agent workflows spanning code generation, question answering, and mathematical reasoning, using the same priorities for prompt optimization and model upgrades. Optimizing the selected agents' prompts achieves a macro-average gain of 3.81 percentage points, compared with 1.85 for uniform agent selection. Across five target models, upgrading the selected agents yields macro-average gains of 7.62-16.42 percentage points, compared with 3.81-8.62 for uniform agent selection. Despite its probing overhead, IF-MAP reduces Qwen3-8B and DeepSeek-V3.2 token use by 74.2% and 35.2%, respectively, relative to optimizing every agent, and reduces target-model tokens by 63.6-64.9% relative to upgrading every agent. These results support the use of IF-MAP to identify promising agents and direct improvement effort toward greater end-to-end performance gains.
items.tldr: IF-MAP priorise les agents dans les systèmes multi-agents LLM via une méthode inspirée des fonctions d'influence, guidant les optimisations (prompts/modèles) pour maximiser le gain systémique avec des ressources limitées.

items.title: BrickWright: Agentic Creation of Physically Feasible Brick Builds
items.summary: Frontier coding agents are becoming increasingly adept at 3D modeling. Yet, they still face challenges when building objects meant to be assembled in the physical world, often creating invalid assemblies with floating, colliding, or disconnected parts. We argue that providing agents with tools for assembling builds and verifying their physical feasibility is sufficient for them to produce physically valid assemblies that still adhere to input prompts. Focusing on the domain of LEGO brick builds, we present BrickWright, a framework for generating physically feasible brick builds from text or image prompts using pre-trained agents, where a build is physically feasible if it uses only real parts, has no colliding or floating parts, and forms a connected structure if possible. BrickWright guides agents to create builds by writing code with BrickLayer, a Python toolkit with two main components: an ergonomic brick assembly API that halves inference cost compared to working in raw LDraw, and a validator that provides feedback on physical feasibility. Whereas baseline agents achieve physical validity rates ranging from only 9% (GPT-6 Luna) to 69% (GPT-6 Astra), BrickWright-guided agents achieve 100% validity on a sample of 512 prompts, while improving prompt adherence for lightweight agents and maintaining it for stronger agents. Additionally, they outperform specialized models on the text-to-brick task. Code is available on our project page: https://avalovelace1.github.io/brickwright/
items.tldr: BrickWright guide les agents IA pour générer des constructions LEGO physiquement valides via un outil de validation et une API d'assemblage, améliorant la faisabilité physique de 9% à 99% selon les modèles. Intéressant pour l'automatisation 3D.

items.title: amitshekhariitbhu/ai-system-design
items.summary: AI System Design - Learn how to design AI systems built on LLMs, RAG, and AI Agents step by step.
items.tldr: Ressource pédagogique détaillée sur la conception de systèmes IA basés sur LLM, RAG et agents, avec des étapes pratiques et des exemples concrets.

items.title: RTAformer: Relation-Transition-Aware Transformer for Video Scene Graph Generation
items.summary: Video scene graph generation (VidSGG) aims to capture objects and their evolving relationships in videos. This requires accounting for both the persistence of object identities and abrupt changes in relationships. Existing methods aggregate information across frames to exploit temporal context, but an emphasis on consistency can obscure these changes. As a result, a model may retain its previous prediction even after the underlying relation has changed. We refer to this failure mode as relational semantic inertia. To address this issue, we propose Relation-Transition-Aware Transformer (RTAformer), a one-stage framework that separately models entity persistence and relation changes. It injects calibrated differences between adjacent-frame relation queries to guide predicate updates, while cross-frame instance alignment during training helps reduce cross-frame representational drift. Experiments on Action Genome show improvements in recall and mean recall over existing methods, with ablation studies supporting the contributions of the proposed components and comparisons using matched backbones showing larger gains on relation-transition frames than on non-transition frames.
items.tldr: Modèle RTAformer pour la génération de graphes de scènes vidéo (VidSGG), adressant l'inertie sémantique relationnelle via des différences calibrées entre trames adjacentes et un alignement croisé des instances. Améliore les métriques de rappel sur Action Genome.

items.title: EvalResearchBench: Can AI Agents Build Their Own Feedback for Recursive Self-Improvement?
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) relies on evaluation feedback to assess progress and guide further research, yet repeatedly running complex benchmarks is costly and slows iteration. Human experts reduce this cost by selecting benchmark subsets or designing compact suites. We ask whether AI agents can automate this design process and introduce EvalResearchBench (ERB), a benchmark for autonomous evaluation research. Given target materials, development references, candidate APIs, and fixed time and API budgets, an agent called the researcher selects or synthesizes tasks, implements graders, and revises them in pilot tests before freezing an executable evaluator for coding, co-work, and reasoning. We study 9 researchers and 13 candidate models and compare each frozen evaluator with 14 target benchmarks on score concordance and pairwise agreement. The best evaluators order about 75\% of candidate pairs as the targets do, below the 91\% ceiling set by disagreements among the targets. No researcher leads on every metric, and the best evaluator on development targets is not the best on sealed targets hidden from the researcher. A human-designed sample of public tasks remains a strong baseline, and the evaluator with the lowest recorded execution cost attains the highest pairwise agreement. Agents repair tasks and graders through pilot feedback, yet their evaluators can still truncate answers, exhaust the evaluation budget, or let a few questions dominate a domain score.
items.tldr: EvalResearchBench explore si des agents IA peuvent concevoir leurs propres benchmarks pour l'auto-amélioration récursive, en comparant des évaluateurs autonomes à des benchmarks humains. Utile pour l'optimisation des processus d'évaluation automatisée.

items.title: Bridging Exploration and Persona: Information-Directed Dueling for Test-Time Agent Personalization
items.summary: Effective test-time personalization requires LLM agents to adapt to query-dependent user preferences from lightweight interaction. We study persona selection with binary comparisons between candidate responses as the online signal. We present ID-TAP, a scalable, IDS-inspired neural dueling-bandit framework for large discrete persona spaces. ID-TAP combines a query-conditioned neural utility model with a lightweight Bradley-Terry explorer, and transfers comparison evidence across related queries through similarity-weighted warm starts. The neural model shares statistical strength across queries while preserving query-specific scores, and efficient BT updates score hypothetical challengers. Across seven user-conditioned generation benchmarks under reference- and model-based preference simulators, ID-TAP achieves the strongest aggregate performance among the evaluated baselines within a fixed ten-round comparison budget. These results support information-directed challenger selection as an effective design for test-time persona adaptation.
items.tldr: ID-TAP utilise un bandit duel inspiré des fonctions d'influence pour personnaliser les agents LLM en temps réel via des comparaisons binaires, améliorant l'adaptation aux préférences utilisateur sous budget limité.

items.title: HyperDrone: Simulation-to-Reality Transfer at Millions of Frames per Second
items.summary: We present HyperDrone, an extremely fast quadrotor simulator focused on high-performance batch rendering that is more than 20x faster than existing state-of-the-art batch quadrotor simulators. HyperDrone combines highly optimized multirotor dynamics with HyperLux, a new ray-tracing engine that supports Nvidia OptiX, Vulkan, Apple Metal and WebGPU backends that takes full advantage of modern ray-tracing hardware, capable of running both components entirely on the GPU. HyperLux renders RGB, depth, semantic/instance segmentation, surface normals and optical flow observations at configurable levels of fidelity, including reflections, realistic lighting, motion blur, anti-aliasing, and Physically Based Rendering (PBR). Even in the highest-fidelity settings, HyperLux achieves millions of Frames Per Second (FPS) on consumer-grade GPUs while rendering realistic 3D scenes. We demonstrate the merits of HyperDrone by training a vision-based yaw-control policy purely in simulation and transferring it to a real small-scale quadrotor (Crazyflie) with a camera, running completely onboard.
items.tldr: HyperDrone accélère les simulations pour drones (20x plus rapide) via un moteur de ray-tracing optimisé (HyperLux), permettant un transfert simulation-réalité à des millions d'images/seconde. Pertinent pour la robotique temps réel.

items.title: FilmFlow: Agentic System for 3D Virtual Film Cinematography
items.summary: Complex camera motion is central to visual storytelling, yet translating cinematographic intent into controllable, executable camera trajectories remains challenging. We introduce FilmFlow, an agentic framework that converts natural-language instructions or reference videos into explicit camera trajectories for dynamic 3D environments. To generate these trajectories, a Director agent constructs executable camera plans by composing high-level motions from concurrent atomic operations that jointly control translation, rotation, and framing. The Director is supported by three specialized agents: an Interpreter that extracts scene-grounded cinematographic intent, a Scout that selects initial viewpoints, and a Critic that evaluates rendered results and provides visual feedback for iterative plan refinement. We also introduce CinemaBench, comprising 150 Blender scenes from self-created and licensed sources, with five camera instructions per scene for 750 text-directed tasks and 60 reference videos associated with a subset of scenes. CinemaBench supports evaluation of both text-directed camera generation and video reference-directed camera generation. Across a diverse set of evaluated baselines, FilmFlow achieves the strongest benchmark performance and the highest user preference, demonstrating effective spatial reasoning, temporal coordination, and visual composition for executable 3D cinematography.
items.tldr: Framework agentique (FilmFlow) pour générer des trajectoires de caméra 3D à partir de consignes textuelles ou de vidéos de référence, avec un benchmark (CinemaBench) de 750 tâches. Démontre la capacité des agents à traduire des intentions cinématographiques en mouvements contrôlables.

items.title: AnyGameRenderer: Entity-Consistent Generative Rendering Across Games and an Entity-Level Benchmark
items.summary: AI coding agents can now build small playable games in minutes, but the results usually look like programmer art: gray blockouts, colored geometric primitives, and flat semantic blobs. We present AnyGameRenderer, a video-to-video generative renderer that turns such footage into high-quality visuals with characters, motion detail, and effects. Throughout, it keeps the layout, camera, and every entity's position and timing intact. Our AnyGameRenderer generalizes across a wide range of genres that agents build, such as tower defense, auto-battlers, top-down survivors, turn-based battles, kart racing, and crowd runners. AnyGameRenderer takes plain video as its game-state input, with no complex representations such as engine G-buffers, per-object class labels, or low-poly proxies. Gray blockouts, colored primitives, semantic maps, and wireframes all work as input. It also preserves entity correspondence: group counts stay correct, and entities appear and disappear on the right frame. We implement AnyGameRenderer by LoRA fine-tuning MiniMax-H3 ref2va, a 33B reference-video-conditioned video generation model. Training uses sim10k paired clips from three sources: (i) multi-stream rendering data from 38 agent-made games exported from GEAR, an AI game-creation tool; (ii) two-stream rendering data from Unreal Engine, with programmatically controlled crowds, count changes, and entity scales; and (iii) real gameplay recordings, with pairs reconstructed via 3D-box detection. To evaluate the entity correspondence, we propose an entity-level benchmark of 59 held-out cases with 753 entities, scored against ground-truth boxes. Compared with the base model, AnyGameRenderer better preserves entity correspondence: temporal match rises from 50.9\% to 62.9\%, missed count changes fall from 34.7\% to 21.3\%, and fewer entities are hallucinated or left unrendered.
items.tldr: AnyGameRenderer transforme des vidéos de jeux générés par IA (blockouts, primitives) en rendus visuels de haute qualité tout en préservant la cohérence des entités et des caméras, généralisant à plusieurs genres de jeux. Basé sur un modèle de génération vidéo conditionnée (MiniMax-H3), il comble le fossé entre génération brute et rendu réaliste.

items.title: Verus-Insight: Towards Explainable Artifact Detection in AI-Generated Videos
items.summary: Recent advances in video generation have made synthetic videos increasingly realistic, placing greater demands on reliable AI-generated video detection. Existing artifact-based detectors typically identify generation artifacts as evidence for source prediction, yet they may either fail to recognize subtle artifacts or reach the correct source decision without faithfully identifying the evidence underlying it. In this work, we systematically investigate how to design and train effective artifact detectors and formulate artifact detection as a structured process comprising three complementary capabilities: Inspection Planning, which determines what should be examined; Evidence Verification, which verifies whether the inspected content exhibits genuine generation artifacts; and Evidence Aggregation, which integrates the verified evidence into the final source decision. Building on this formulation, we introduce Verus-Insight, trained with human-anchored full-process supervision and progressive capability training to strengthen both fine-grained artifact detection and video-level detection. We further introduce Verus-Bench, a benchmark with fine-grained human annotations of perceptible artifacts for evaluating artifact detection. Extensive experiments across diverse benchmarks demonstrate that Verus-Insight achieves strong performance in both fine-grained artifact analysis and AI-generated video detection, with substantial gains in recovering human-perceived artifacts. Further analyses reveal that the three capabilities are complementary yet distinct, and that Verus-Insight more reliably converts relevant inspection targets into supported artifact evidence without increasing spurious artifact claims.
items.tldr: Verus-Insight formalise la détection d'artefacts dans les vidéos générées par IA en trois étapes (planification, vérification, agrégation) et introduit Verus-Bench, un benchmark avec annotations fines. Le modèle détecte des artefacts subtils et fournit des explications structurées pour la source des vidéos.

items.title: Cola2: Co-Adaptive Hierarchical Language Modeling with Continuous Semantic Compression and Balanced Discrete Generation
items.summary: Hierarchical language generation separates continuous semantic modeling from discrete text realization, but its effectiveness depends on what the latent space compresses and how the discrete generator uses it. We propose Cola2, a framework that jointly studies continuous semantic compression, the balance between reconstruction and generation, and continuous-discrete co-adaptation. Cola2 dynamically segments text into semantic spans, controls the compression rate through auxiliary-loss-free negative feedback, and combines reconstruction and generation supervision to learn compact, predictive latent representations. A block-causal masked diffusion decoder is trained with clean, noisy, and dropped latent conditions, while classifier-free guidance adjusts the balance between semantic reconstruction and autonomous generation. Token-prediction gradients update the encoder through the latents, whereas Flow Matching prior learning is decoupled from representation learning by stop-gradient. During inference, generated text is re-encoded under a fixed span layout to keep the latent history consistent with the actual text context. Experiments on five downstream tasks with about 210 billion training tokens validate the core designs and show competitive, unsaturated scaling. With 346.03 billion source tokens, an unconverged checkpoint reaches a 60.10 average across eight tasks and surpasses Llama-3-8B on HellaSwag and StoryCloze despite its reported pretraining budget being over 43 times larger. These results demonstrate the potential of continuous-latent hierarchical language generation.
items.tldr: Cola2 explore une génération hiérarchique de langage avec compression sémantique continue et génération discrète équilibrée, combinant reconstruction et supervision générative. Les représentations latentes compactes améliorent les performances sur 5 tâches aval avec 210B de tokens.

items.title: Harvil1/codeAgent
items.summary: CodeAgent is an open-source coding agent that lives in your terminal. It understands your repository, plans multi-step changes, writes and edits files, runs commands and tests, and iterates until the task is done — all with a transparent, extensible tool loop.
items.tldr: Agent de codage autonome (Python) exécuté en terminal, planifiant et exécutant des modifications multi-étapes dans un dépôt. Démontre l'autonomie des agents mais manque de benchmarks comparatifs ou de validation académique.

items.title: Realism VS Accuracy: Event Sequence Forecasting from a Generative Modeling Perspective
items.summary: Event sequences are chains of random events, each described by heterogeneous (numerical and categorical) features. The problem of event sequence forecasting occurs in finance, healthcare, business process intelligence, and other fields. In this work, we study multi-horizon forecasting of event sequences as a conditional generative modeling problem. We evaluate forecasts not only for prediction accuracy, but also for distributional realism. To this end, we present a benchmark comprising metrics for both quality aspects, strong statistical baselines, recent models adapted from adjacent fields, and curated real-world datasets. Careful evaluation reveals that no method excels at both accuracy and realism, highlighting a fundamental trade-off between the two. Finally, we introduce Wasserstein BaryBooster, an algorithm that aggregates samples from a realism-strong diffusion model into a state-of-the-art predictor, demonstrating that distributional realism can be converted into prediction accuracy. Code is available at https://github.com/xaosina/event-sequence-forecasting.
items.tldr: Benchmark et modèle (Wasserstein BaryBooster) pour évaluer la précision et le réalisme des séquences d'événements, révélant un compromis fondamental entre les deux. Application en finance, santé et gestion de processus.
